world_identity: journal_id plus deterministic digest of captured sources, declared scope, analyzer versions, rules and decisions; repeated identical analysis reuses the version
rule_scope: all_sections only when explicitly supported by a supplied guideline or a template-wide candidate; per-template-section observations do not imply manuscript section correspondence
source_assurance: operator_supplied; deterministic recognition of explicit requirements does not authenticate a publisher or prove the supplied guide is current
source_semantics: Captured sources are immutable and retained with exact hashes and locators.
Template formatting produces candidate expectations, never normative requirements by itself.
Only explicitly supported unambiguous guideline patterns can be confirmed by deterministic extraction.
Unparsed text, mixed section geometry, unsupported input and absent properties remain explicit coverage gaps.
Shared components are declarative data with exact versions and per-journal applicability evidence; no dynamic imports, eval, commands or script execution.
New world storage validates captured source bytes and reproduces analysis plus the ordered local decisions; a self-consistent manifest hash alone cannot authorize invented rules.

PDF guidance feeds the same narrow deterministic requirement recognizer as text guidance, with page/block evidence locators; conditional, negative or unparsed blocks remain explicit gaps and never become confirmed rules.

Page-format definition sentences (for example 'A double column page is defined as a 7.875″ x 10.75″ page') yield the column count and page dimensions; qualifiers in the same sentence without a checkable geometry property are carried as rule limitations.
check_semantics: An applicable confirmed expectation produces compliant only when every required section is observed and matches; a known mismatch produces violation even when other section values are missing.
Every rule result exposes applicability separately as APPLICABLE, NOT_APPLICABLE or UNKNOWN.
Candidate comparisons produce observed_match or observed_difference, never violation.
A candidate mismatch produces observed_difference even when other section values are missing; observed_match requires complete matching section coverage.
A conflict or incomplete coverage with no known mismatch remains cannot_determine; an unsupported scope remains not_checked. Per-section observations and missing coverage are preserved separately.
Checks bind immutable manuscript baseline, world version and checker dependencies.
A newer world only creates update_available; it does not stale a check still bound to unchanged inputs.

Changing a binding, source baseline, analyzer, reader or checker version makes the retained check STALE; historical conclusions remain intact. Corrupt retained source or world evidence is a read failure, never a fabricated current result.
Disposition records do not change check verdicts or rule confirmation.

result_axes.derivation: The four independent presentation axes are rule basis, check verdict, current validity and operator disposition; applicability is an additional separate scope result. Dispositions are immutable records, not edits to any other axis.

persistence: The retained world record is the single authority. New checks persist world_version_id and explicit dependencies, not an embedded second world.

The service joins the retained world into an HTTP check response for presentation. It derives validity, stale_reasons, update_available and dispositions when reading; those fields are not persisted as check authority.
Source-baseline guards and current-binding validation must still hold at binding and check commits.
Retained world source bytes, check dependencies, binding references and content hashes are verified before reuse.
historical_access: A supported retained world schema can be read after its analyzer method changes; historical access does not re-execute or restore that older analyzer.
A new check or local rule correction requires the current analyzer and DOCX reader semantics; re-import captured sources to create a current version instead of relabeling an old world.
Retained checker 1.0.0 records keep their original missing-value aggregation and absent per-finding verdicts. They are validated as historical records, not generated by an active legacy checker.
New checks require checker 1.1.0 and the current DOCX reader. A historical embedded world is verified against its retained identity; new writes reject world duplication.
presentation: Rule bubbles expose separate verdict, basis, validity and disposition axes. Formal violations, candidate differences, undetermined rules and unchecked rules are counted separately.

Source-material coverage_gaps and manuscript missing observations are distinct counts. A manuscript missing observation is one returned section/property finding whose observed value is null; an unexecuted conflicting rule does not fabricate missing findings.
STALE results retain their historical conclusion but never use the current compliant appearance.
Rule evidence and manuscript section observations are shown side by side. A manual resolution displays its reason, actor and previous-to-selected value alongside unchanged original evidence quotes.

Version comparisons expose changes in expectation, basis, scope, unit, evidence and resolution; same-value rules with different applicability or provenance are not presented as identical requirements.
No full-journal compliance claim is made from page-geometry checks alone.

Source document edits and publication actions do not occur in this slice. LibreOffice headless PDF rendering is available only through an explicit capability-gated operation and does not create page mappings.
Source review fragments retain stable source-bound identity, parent hierarchy and exact text spans. Suggestions never become rule evidence solely through similarity.
Text vector similarity is an explainable retrieval score, not a neural embedding, calibrated probability, or compliance verdict. It never merges components or alters retained worlds.
World, component, rule, source and manuscript observations are separately addressable review levels with return navigation.
Manuscript reading exposes every supported object type, region filters, continuation, exact saved responses, historical baselines and explicit retained page evidence.
revision_rules: A local rule correction creates a new world version and records base version, rule, value, reason and actor.
The old world and checks remain immutable; project bindings do not move automatically.
Disposition actions are note or defer and retain the original check verdict.

session.asset_identity: SHA-256 of the route-named static byte snapshots captured when the server starts; it does not claim the running server reflects later source edits.
session.client_behavior: Refuse an unsupported HTTP contract. A changed asset_version requires a page reload before more mutations. Restart the service to load changed static assets.

requests.semantics: Analyze a captured rule component and optional captured sources with all retained sources of the selected world. Carry prior operator decisions, then apply explicit operator-confirmed decisions, and save one immutable version. preview=true returns the analyzed world without saving sources or a version. Imported declarations remain candidates unless an existing confirmed guide or operator decision determines the same property. Existing manuscript bindings are unchanged. Invalid input saves nothing.
Return the exact retained DOCX bytes for one explicit baseline without reading an author path or recording a structured read receipt.

field_semantics.name: Manuscript display label; it does not have to end in .docx.
field_semantics.filename: Original manuscript basename with .docx extension, never a filesystem path.
field_semantics.content_base64: Captured file bytes; the HTTP API never accepts an author input path.
field_semantics.journal_name: Journal display name in world records and state summaries; no name alias.
field_semantics.expected_binding_id: Explicit null for the initial binding, otherwise the current binding identity used for compare-and-swap.
field_semantics.expected: Integer in the rule's stored unit: twips for dimensions and margins, count for columns.
field_semantics.baseline_id: GET manuscript accepts current or an exact retained baseline ID; POST read accepts explicit null for current or a retained ID. Render operations require exact retained baseline IDs.
field_semantics.render_bundle_id: Explicit retained render evidence selection for a physical-page query; null for source object queries.
field_semantics.query: All six fields are present. Selectors/cursor are nullable; page_size is a positive bounded integer enforced by ReadQuery.
field_semantics.request_id: A stable per-submission kebab-case identity for recoverable baseline updates. Replay returns the same saved outcome.
field_semantics.libreoffice_executable: Absolute path to the explicitly selected LibreOffice executable. Missing or non-LibreOffice capabilities return code renderer_unavailable with no fallback.
field_semantics.libreoffice_profile: Not accepted over HTTP. The service creates a private temporary profile below its selected library var/libreoffice-profile directory for every render.
field_semantics.render_record/page_index/pdf/document_an: Each supplied upload contains only content_base64. Annotation and page evidence are both null or both supplied. Uploaded historical paths are never opened.
field_semantics.pages: Captured page PNG bytes with explicit unique positive page_number, validated against the original index and physical PDF.

failure_rules: POST bodies require their exact declared keys, application/json and a unique bounded Content-Length; malformed input is not converted to empty success.
GET query parameters must exactly match the declared query_fields; unknown or repeated parameters return HTTP 400.
Binding compare-and-swap conflicts return HTTP 409; invalid local origin or session returns 403.

Baseline rendering returns HTTP 503 with code renderer_unavailable when the selected LibreOffice executable is absent or does not identify as LibreOffice, and HTTP 502 with code render_failed after a failed conversion or unreadable PDF. No fallback renderer is attempted.
Storage corruption and internal persistence failures return a generic HTTP 500 without local paths or database details; unsupported methods return JSON HTTP 405 with an Allow header.
The frontend rejects malformed response records and commits a refreshed view only after all required reads succeed.
If a write succeeded but the following refresh failed, report the saved operation explicitly and require refresh instead of encouraging a duplicate submission.
http.read_response: Unmodified persistent project response and actual-read receipt; discovery remains catalog_only.
http.binary_response: GET /api/render returns exactly the selected retained PDF or PNG, verified against the bundle. page_number is none for PDF and a positive number for a PNG.

runtime_boundary: Local operator workbench; session and origin checks do not provide remote user authentication.

source_review.relation_score: lexical cosine in [0,1], retrieval ranking only; no probability, merging or compliance inference
source_review.pdf_fragment_binding: PDF fragment identifiers bind pdf_source_version instead of the DOCX reader version; bbox values are PDF points with a top-left origin.
